item.title: Haris Rauf punished for on-field confrontation during Pakistan's win over England
item.description: Pakistan fast bowler Haris Rauf has been fined 20 per cent of his match fee and received a demerit point for his on-field behaviour during Sunday's ODI against England in Lahore. The visitors were also penalised after failing to maintain the required over-rate. The International Cricket Council (ICC) confirmed that Rauf breached Article 2.2 of its Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which covers conduct contrary to the spirit of the game. He received an official reprimand, taking his tally to five demerit points following his third offence within a 24-month period. The incident occurred towards the end of Pakistan's innings, after the 46th over, when Rauf was at the non-striker's end. The pacer appealed for a wide before getting into an argument with England all-rounder Will Jacks. Rauf raised his bat during the exchange and continued the argument despite being warned by umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid. He then brushed past the umpire while moving towards Jacks. England were handed a separate penalty, with their players fined 15 per cent of their match fees for maintaining an over-rate three overs below the required level, even after time allowances were taken into account. The sanction was imposed under Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct, which provides for a five per cent fine on players' match fees for every over a team falls short of the minimum over-rate requirement. Both Rauf and England captain Harry Brook accepted the charges and the penalties proposed by Jeff Crowe of the Emirates ICC Elite Panel of Match Referees. As a result, neither case required a formal hearing. The charges against the two teams were brought by on-field umpires Rashid Riaz and Sharfuddoula, third umpire Wayne Knights and fourth umpire Nassir Hussain. The disciplinary action followed a dramatic contest in which Pakistan secured a one-wicket victory while chasing England's total. Shadab Khan played a decisive role with an unbeaten century to keep Pakistan in the hunt during the closing stages. Shadab and Rauf then stitched together an unbroken 89-run partnership for the final wicket to take Pakistan over the line with 17 balls remaining. The victory also booked Pakistan's place in the ODI tri-series final, where they are scheduled to face Sri Lanka on October 31.

item.title: Alex Freeman: Man United set to clash with PL rival in ferocious January transfer battle
item.description: Alex Freeman: Man United set to clash with PL rival in ferocious January transfer battle A defensive rebuild tops Manchester United’s agenda in 2027. Beyond the club’s clear defensive struggles, Ineos has already earmarked the back line as the next priority in its transfer strategy. The last two summers saw the attack and midfield strengthened in turn; now the defence is next. Several United defenders may need to make way for these reinforcements, and Diogo Dalot is among those most likely to depart. Reports last week indicated that Dalot could leave next year should the Red Devils fail to secure Champions League football. Given United’s wretched start to the season, a top-four or top-five finish looks increasingly improbable. Serie A’s heavyweights are already circling, so the Portuguese full-back walking away is a real prospect. Dalot departs, Freeman arrives If Dalot leaves, United will need a replacement. According to TeamTalk , Villarreal’s American full-back Alex Freeman has emerged as a leading candidate. “We can confirm that Manchester United scouts have checked on Freeman in recent weeks,” the outlet reports. Yet Ineos will not have the field to itself. Tottenham Hotspur also admire the 22-year-old and view him as a long-term successor to Pedro Porro, who has been linked with moves to Barcelona or Real Madrid next year. Meanwhile, Manchester City and Chelsea are also monitoring the right-back closely. What sets Freeman apart The USMNT international stands out through a rare blend of defensive versatility, elite athleticism and composure on the biggest stages of European and international football. Since his winter 2026 move to Europe, he has flourished, impressing at the World Cup and looking every inch a player built for the Premier League’s intensity. However, with Freeman tied to Villarreal until 2032, he will not be a straightforward acquisition. item.title: Ulster trio sign contract extensions until 2029
item.description: Baloucoune, McNabney and Hopes have all signed new deals until "at least" the summer of 2029 [Getty Images] Robert Baloucoune, James McNabney and Joe Hopes have signed contract extensions with Ulster. Ireland wing Baloucoune, 29, has penned fresh terms after a memorable 2026 in which his eye-catching Six Nations displays earned him the championship's Rising Player award. Back rower McNabney's new deal comes a week after he was called up to the Ireland squad, with the 23-year-old having made his Ulster return last month following a year out with a serious knee injury. Versatile forward Hopes, who can play at lock or in the back row, has also committed his future after breaking into the senior team last season. The 2022 Ulster Schools' player of the year made his debut aged 19 in 2023 and featured off the bench in the Challenge Cup win over Zebre earlier this month. Ulster say all three have signed new deals until "at least" the summer of 2029. "We are delighted to have secured the futures of Rob, James and Joe," said Ulster general manager Rory Best. "Rob has showcased his importance to this Ulster team and the national team with his abilities and performances. He is a test-level winger who has really benefitted from a run of games over the past year. "Both James and Joe are working hard in the early stages of their professional careers and have both shown a lot of potential in our forward pack." Best added: "Everyone here was delighted to see James called up to the Ireland squad after the adversity he faced coming back from a long-term knee injury. "We have full belief that all three will form an important part of our Ulster team in the coming years and look forward to seeing what they produce on the field."

item.title: Milwaukee Bucks find first win while Giannis Antetokounmpo’s winless-Heat struggle
item.description: Giannis Antetokounmpo’s blockbuster move brought an end to months of speculation about his future and the Milwaukee Bucks’ next steps. The two time MVP sought a better opportunity to compete for a championship elsewhere, while Milwaukee shifted its focus toward accelerating a rebuild. Yet after four games, the Bucks and the Heat were heading in very different directions, defying what many basketball fans had expected. Miami’s struggles continued with a fourth straight loss , as the Heat surrendered a six point advantage in the final quarter against the Dallas Mavericks. Milwaukee, on the other hand, came away with a 110-102 win against the Indiana Pacers, with Tyrese Haliburton leading the charge. The contrasting results add an unexpected twist to the situation, especially when considering the performances of the Bucks’ main contributors. The Milwaukee Bucks finally find their first dub Tyler Herro paced the Bucks on Tuesday with 23 points, 10 rebounds, seven assists, one steal, and one block in 32 minutes, while knocking down three shots from beyond the arc. Kel’el Ware also made an impact as a reserve, finishing with 16 points, 14 rebounds, and one steal in just 19 minutes on 7 of 13 shooting. Giannis put together an impressive all around showing for Miami, finishing with 29 points, 14 boards, 11 assists, and a block while sinking two triples. Bam Adebayo, however, couldn’t match his teammate’s production. In 30 minutes, the All Star center posted eight points, eight rebounds, three assists, two steals, and two blocks, shooting just 3 of 10 from the floor and going 0 for 5 from long range. His early season numbers have also been modest, with Adebayo averaging 11.8 points and converting only 16.7 percent of his three point attempts over his past four outings. item.title: The 2026 Awful Announcing sports podcast power list
item.description: Edit by Liam McGuire When we published our first sports podcast power list at Awful Announcing in 2024, we imagined capturing the energy around what we then called a “cottage industry.” Sports may be just a subset of the exploding podcast space, but its growth has been remarkable in that time . Though the nine-figure mega-deals from buyers like SiriusXM, Amazon, and Spotify slowed in 2026, this year was marked by consolidation around industry-defining hits. With fewer breakout podcasts or new star hosts, the best are in an arms race for distribution and business opportunities. That starts with streaming. The expected boon for podcasters from the Netflix-YouTube war may be weaker than we thought this time last year, but that standoff will still change the space. Beneficiaries like The Ringer and Barstool already have benefited . And based on Netflix’s deal-making, we are learning which shows might work for a streamer and which will not. YouTube boosted its view counts, but it also pushed viewers more toward well-produced content and new, more sellable “shows.” The creative deployment of podcast hosts and creators in traditional sports programming is already clear across ESPN and Prime Video’s lineup. Past honorees from this list, such as Pat McAfee, Bussin’ With the Boys , Josh Pate, and the crew behind the old JJ Redick podcast, are examples . The windfall from sports gambling can no longer sustain entire podcast businesses. The big books — and smaller companies like Underdog — have cut their original programming. But recently, prediction markets and AI companies have begun throwing money at podcasting, and they could spark a similar wave of spending that propels other podcasts to new heights. What looks like a maturing industry from one angle also threatens the creative excitement that led audiences to jump from radio or television to podcasts in the first place. A day still has just 24 hours, so existing hits prevent new ones. Fresh, exciting content will have to come from the established power players. So far, indicators suggest they are up for it. New “off the couch” formats from digital players like Playmaker and Wave, the embrace of “IRL” (in real life) live content and events, and continued experiments that blur the lines between television and podcasts could generate the next hit from within well-known IP. Amid this curious moment in sports podcasting and digital video, here is the third annual Awful Announcing Sports Podcast Power List. item.description: Sep 5, 2026; Fayetteville, Arkansas, USA; Arkansas Razorbacks head coach Ryan Silverfield during warmups prior to the game against the North Alabama Lions at Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nelson Chenault-Imag… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kate Pearson Halyburton, Editor Arkansas does not have to love the Battle Line Rivalry. It does need a better response than losing and explaining why Missouri was never the preferred rival anyway. That argument has become too comfortable for a matchup that keeps producing uncomfortable results. Razorback Ledger: Arkansas Can’t Keep Losing to Missouri The Losses Are Not Irrelevant Missouri has won four consecutive meetings and 10 of the 12 annual SEC matchups played from 2014 through 2025. The Tigers do not need unanimous approval from Razorback fans to make those victories count. They have taken the results while Arkansas has spent too much time debating the relationship. Saturday in Fayetteville gives the Razorbacks a chance to change that. It also offers a less flattering possibility: another defeat, followed by another discussion about why the opponent shouldn’t matter this much. At some point, dismissing Missouri stops sounding like indifference and starts sounding like an escape from the comparison. The Rivalry Debate Has Become a Convenient Escape Nobody can order a fan base to feel something. Arkansas has older football relationships, deeper grudges, and memories no trophy announcement can manufacture. Missouri’s place on the annual schedule did not obligate Razorback fans to rearrange their emotional priorities. But emotional investment and competitive responsibility are different subjects. A conference loss does not become less damaging because the opponent lacks the preferred history. Missouri has repeatedly taken a game Arkansas needed and added it to its own record. The Razorbacks won the annual SEC series in 2015 and 2021. Missouri won ten other meetings. Fans can dislike the branding while acknowledging that the football has become a recurring problem. Those positions are entirely compatible. What does not hold up is treating the matchup as beneath Arkansas’ attention while the Tigers keep controlling the outcome. Competitive standing isn’t decided by which opponent deserves respect. It is established by what happens when the teams play. item.title: Unlucky seven? Wrexham aim to buck bizarre trend
item.description: Wrexham have won just three of their 12 Championship matches so far this season [Getty Images] Phil Parkinson is hoping Wrexham can buck the unusual trend of Championship sides struggling in seasons after they have narrowly missed out on the play-offs. Over the previous 15 second-tier campaigns, only one side have achieved a top-half finish - when Middlesbrough came fourth in 2022-23 - in the year after finishing seventh in the Championship. Wrexham ended up seventh last season - the club's highest ever league finish - as they lost out on a top-six place following a 2-2 draw with Boro on the final day. The Red Dragons currently sit 17th having claimed just 14 of the 36 points on offer so far this season. "I think that there's obviously a stat of teams who've been in the play-offs can find it tough, but you look at Derby, they just missed out as well, how they've struggled," said Parkinson. "Whether that [mental toughness] is a factor or not... Of course, as much as there was a pride that in our first season in the Championship we'd got to seventh, the highest position the club had ever finished, on the last day of the season there was an opportunity which slipped away from us. "But it's up to us to buck the trend of that." Parkinson's gratitude as Wrexham boss hits landmark Gudjohnsen double gives Blackburn win over Wrexham Despite Wrexham's slow start to the campaign, they have the same number of points now as they did at the same stage last term. Parkinson's team are bidding to respond to last weekend's 2-0 loss at Blackburn Rovers when they return to action against Sheffield United at Bramall Lane on Friday (20:00 GMT). The Blades fixture comes almost exactly five years on from the day co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac attended their first Wrexham match. The Hollywood pair watched on as Parkinson's side - then in the National League - were beaten 3-2 at Maidenhead United in October 2021. Having masterminded three promotions and the club's highest-ever league finish since being appointed in the summer of 2021, Parkinson stated that Wrexham's upcoming opponents serve as a reminder of the immense progress made during his tenure. item.description: Michael Carrick makes Bruno Fernandes selection decision for Chelsea after clear-the-air talks Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is likely to start against Chelsea on Saturday after holding clear-the-air talks with head coach Michael Carrick. How the Como fallout escalated The dispute began when Fernandes questioned United’s decision not to press man-to-man after the 4-1 defeat at Como on 21 October. Carrick responded by criticising the players’ work rate before leaving his captain on the bench throughout Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth, after which Fernandes liked an Instagram post referring to loyalty and no longer caring. Carrick and Fernandes clear the air at Carrington Carrick has now spoken to Fernandes face to face, separately from a wider meeting involving the squad and first-team staff on Tuesday. The pair have cleared the air and are determined to move forward (via The Telegraph ). Fernandes also attended Carrington for treatment on Monday, despite most of the squad having the day off. Staff are said to have been encouraged by his response and believe they have seen “the best version of Fernandes over the last two days”. Carrick considers the disciplinary episode closed and is expected to recall the Portuguese at Stamford Bridge, provided his ongoing fitness issue does not intervene. Fernandes was pictured in good spirits during Wednesday morning’s training session. United are seeking only their second Premier League victory of the campaign and sit one point above the relegation zone. Kobbie Mainoo returned to training on Wednesday after missing four matches, but Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw, Benjamin Sesko and Patrick Dorgu are among the players who have been sidelined. Six years as United’s creative leader Fernandes joined United from Sporting CP on 30 January 2020 for an initial £47 million, with add-ons capable of increasing the fee to £67.7 million. He made his debut against Wolverhampton Wanderers two days later. The midfielder has recorded 74 goals in 235 Premier League appearances for the Red Devils. He was appointed permanent club captain in July 2023 and has never left United on loan. Fernandes helped the club win the 2022/23 League Cup and the 2023/24 FA Cup. His current contract runs until June 2027 and includes an option for a further season. A return to the starting XI at Chelsea is now the most likely outcome, but Fernandes’ influence will need to translate quickly into a better collective performance as pressure continues to build on Carrick. Final Thoughts Fernandes and Carrick have held clear-the-air talks following the captain’s Bournemouth omission. United staff have been encouraged by Fernandes’ response at Carrington. The midfielder is likely to start against Chelsea if fit. Kobbie Mainoo has returned to training before Saturday’s trip to Stamford Bridge.

item.title: India series drive record Cricket Australia revenue, two-day Ashes Tests burn A$20m hole in finances
item.description: Cricket Australia's (CA) record revenue of A$601.1 million ($423 million) in the 2025-26 financial year was driven by media rights deals for the Ashes and the limited-overs series against India. The governing body also reported a net surplus of A$81.8 million ($57 million), but two Ashes Tests that ended inside two days last summer cost it an estimated A$20 million in revenue. The financial impact comes as CA prepares for two consecutive years of projected losses, with deficits expected in 2026-27 and 2027-28. On Wednesday, Cricket Australia said its financial results for 2025-26 reflected strong commercial performance, record audiences and the success of the international season. In the previous financial year, 2024-25, it had recorded a net loss of A$11.3 million ($7.95 million). CA said the men's home Ashes series against England and the white-ball series against India generated record media, commercial and match-day revenue. However, it expects revenue to fall over the next two financial years due to a “cyclical decline in media rights and match revenues in line with the international touring schedule.” The financial outlook does not include the anticipated sale of stakes in some Big Bash League (BBL) franchises. Australia's teams also enjoyed success on the field during the year. The men's side retained the Ashes with a 4-1 series win at home, while the women's team won its seventh ICC T20 World Cup title after beating England in the final at Lord's. During October and November last year, Australia won the ODI series against India 2-1, while India claimed the T20I series by the same margin. The Ashes also drew record crowds, with 859,580 spectators attending matches over 18 days, at an average of 47,754 per day. 135263203 Two-day Ashes Tests cost CA A$20 million Despite the record financial results, the two Ashes Tests that ended inside two days dealt a significant blow to CA's revenue. The initial estimate for the loss from the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) Test was A$10 million, but the final impact was higher. The Perth Test, which also failed to reach a third day, added to the shortfall. At Wednesday's annual general meeting, outgoing CA chair Mike Baird joked about the need for future Test matches to last the full five days while addressing his successor, former Australia batter David Boon. “We’ve had a record Ashes crowd at the MCG, 94,000, only going two days there,” Baird said. “Let’s mark it down that five-day Tests are a good thing, Boonie.” The combined revenue hit from the two shortened Tests amounted to A$20 million, adding to the challenges facing CA as it prepares for two years of projected losses.

item.title: Brewers' Pat Murphy Explains Decision To Not Use Jacob Misiorowski In 12th Inning
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy The Tampa Bay Rays walked off the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the World Series in 12 innings. After Cooper Pratt hit a go-ahead home run in the top of the 12th inning, it looked like the Brewers were headed for a celebration for the ages. However, they still had three outs to get. The only problem was that Dustin May, JoJo Romero, Aaron Ashby, Abner Uribe, Trevor Megill and DL Hall had all been used. Manager Pat Murphy left Antonio Senzatela in to face Junior Caminero and he got a ground ball. However, Joey Ortiz made an error, allowing him to reach. He would eventually be lifted for a pinch runner who came around to score the tying run. Senzatela was pulled and replaced with Shane Drohan, who gave up four straight hits to lose the game. With a chance at a championship on the line, many were confused as to why Murphy did not deploy his ace Jacob Misiorowski for the save. In the past, aces have come in to close out big games, and without many options remaining, Misiorowski seemed like a solid choice. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! "You can’t blow that type of situation on a one-run lead on the road,” Murphy said when asked if Misiorowski was an option in extra innings . "If we were in the 13th inning and had a three-run lead, that might be a little bit different, and I probably still wouldn't have." Misiorowski will start Game 5, as he was always slated to do. However, it's clear that Murphy had an eye on the future, thinking about what would happen if the Brewers lost despite Pratt's clutch home run. The question on every fan's mind is why even think about Game 5 if Misiorowski can win Game 4? Did Murphy not trust him? Was he not ready?
